Sentence (English): Our 9 year old Bosch died (springs on the door tore out of their anchors), so we went with this model as a replacement.
Comments (English): [ Sometimes the techie engineers get in the way. ] || ---------------- || Our 9 year old Bosch died (springs on the door tore out of their anchors), so we went with this model as a replacement. Two months or so later we are still wrestling with its operation. No longer is it a matter of the touching power pad, the cleaning cycle pad you want and then the start pad. You now have to program in a cycle which the machine remembers and in order to change cycles you have to go through a multi-step reprogramming process. The fact that the unit is bluetooth enabled seems mildly entertaining but frivolous. The unit cleans quietly and well so far, hence the 4 star rating. Sentence (English): Choosing a dishwasher involved extensive research, with Bosch, LG, Voltas, and Faber initially considered.
Comments (English): [ The Best Dishwasher for Versatility and value ] || ---------------- || Choosing a dishwasher involved extensive research, with Bosch, LG, Voltas, and Faber initially considered. Faber was eliminated due to fewer programs, limited rack adjustment options, overall product finish, and service issues. Voltas was ruled out due to bad reviews, poor material quality, and ordinary looks. LG was discarded after store visits revealed a confusing user interface and unclear steam use, despite all brands generating steam. Bosch and IFB were the finalists. Further research revealed Bosch's plastic bottom, which might cause Odor and dependability issues. Additionally, the Bosch dishwasher was 20% more expensive than IFB and lacked features like auto door opening and Odor removal. Therefore, I chose the IFB Neptune VX16 Dishwasher. Having used the IFB Neptune VX16 for 1 month, I am extremely pleased. It has made life significantly easier, delivering sparkling clean dishes every time without pre-rinsing. The 16-place setting is ideal for my family, accommodating all our dishes, pots, and pans in one go. The Flexi Half Load feature is highly convenient, allowing operation with smaller loads without wasting water and energy. The adjustable upper basket is perfect for fitting larger dishes. The smart programs select the best settings based on the dish's dirtiness, making it user-friendly. It effectively washes all types of utensils, including steel, copper, Silicone, ceramic, bone china, glass, crockery, and dishwasher and microwave-safe items. It handles everything from cooker-kadhai to wine glasses and spoons effortlessly. The auto door opening ensures 100% dry utensils after every wash cycle. The upper cutlery tray allows for separate arrangement of cutlery, making loading and unloading easier. Complete loading takes only 7-8 minutes, and operating the dishwasher is straightforward. Learning to place utensils correctly for optimal cleaning is crucial. Different utensils require varying degrees of cleaning, and proper placement ensures effective results. This understanding comes with multiple washes. The hot wash and rinse instill confidence in the hygiene of my dishes, a reassurance I lacked with a maid. Operating the dishwasher is more cost-effective than hiring a maid. My maid charged Rs 1500 per month, and I anticipate recovering the dishwasher's cost and monthly running expenses within 4-5 years. The average dishwasher life cycle is 8-10 years, suggesting long-term savings. The dishwasher's versatility extends to washing the filter of my chimney. The darker shade and improved front finish are visually appealing. For installation, an inlet water connection, water drain source, and a 16 AMP plug point are needed. Preparing these beforehand ensures a hassle-free and quick installation. IFB provided a prompt installation service. The dishwasher operates quietly, conserves water and energy, and integrates seamlessly into my kitchen. It requires detergent, salt, and rinse-aid, costing approximately Rs 600-650 per month for daily use, or a tablet costing about Rs 750 per month. The IFB Neptune VX16 Dishwasher has been a fantastic addition to my home. It's easy to use and delivers excellent performance. I highly recommend it to anyone seeking a reliable and efficient dishwasher. This product certainly deserves a 5-star rating!

Since it was the weekend, I had to read reviews and watch videos on my own, which was a bit of a struggle. I later called customer service and was able to get the manual right away. However, a problem arose a few days ago. There was water constantly leaking from the front, so I decided to pay more attention to the area next to the sink. Then I noticed a small amount of water leaking from the back, near the water inlet stopper. The manual says to tighten it, so my husband tightened it back up, but it's still leaking a little, so I left a question on the website today. Also, the authentication process keeps saying the serial number is invalid. It's a bit of an inconvenience, separate from the actual use. Nevertheless, I'm satisfied with it. It might be a little small for our three-person household, but it's convenient and easy to clean up. I'm leaving a review after two months of use. ^^ (Additional review regarding after-sales service) I'm leaving this review because I think there might be others who are experiencing the same inconvenience. I contacted Minix for after-sales service due to a water leak, but since it was shipped directly from Hi-Mart, they told me to contact Hi-Mart since it was difficult to confirm, so I just left a 1:1 inquiry. I waited on hold for 20 minutes but couldn't get through, so I ended up leaving an inquiry. Also, please note that this product is an older model that cannot be registered as genuine. Less than a month after I purchased it, a new model was released under the name "Pro," and genuine registration is only possible from that model. Although the after-sales service for this product is applicable from the date of purchase, I feel uneasy because I was told that genuine registration is not possible. Afterwards, I also purchased a dryer, and my affection for Minix products has really fallen away.
Comments (Original): [ 구입하고 싱크대 위 공간에 아주 ] || ---------------- || 구입하고 싱크대 위 공간에 아주 안성맞춤이라 너무 좋았어요. 그리고 설치도 간단하고 여성 혼자도 충분히 할 수 있었답니다. 한가지, 보통 제품 내부에 함께 오는 설명서가 오지 않았고 주말이라 저 혼자 여기저기 후기와 영상 보며 설치하느라 조금 애를 먹었고 나중에 고객센터와 통화하여 바로 설명서도 받을 수 있었어요.그런데 문제는 요며칠 전에 하나 생겼네요. 앞쪽에 자꾸 물이 있어서 싱크볼 옆이니 제가 더 신경써야겠다하고 살폈는데 알고보니 뒤쪽 설치급수마개쪽에서 아주 소량의 물이 새어나오고 있더라구요. 설명서에 꽉 조이라고 되어 있어서 남편이 다시 풀어 꽉 조였는데도 아직도 조금씩 새어나와서 오늘 사이트에 문의 남겨두었어요. 그리고 정품인증도 자꾸 올바르지 않은 시리얼번호라고 나와서 ㅠ.ㅠ 사용과는 별개로 좀 불편을 겪고 있네요.그럼에도 불구하고 사용은 만족합니다. 3인 가구인 저희에겐 조금 작은 듯하지만 그때그때 치우면 편리하고 좋아요. 두달 쓴 후기 남깁니다.^^(AS관련 추가 후기) 저처럼 불편을 겪으시는 분이 계실 것 같아 남깁니다. 누수로 인해 미닉스에 AS를 접수하였더니 하이마트에서 직접 배송한 제품이라 확인이 어려우니 하이마트에 접수하라고 하여 방금 1:1문의에 남겨두었습니다. 20분간 대기했는데도 통화 연결이 안돼서 결국 문의에 남겼습니다. 또한 이 제품은 정품등록이 안되는 이전 제품이라고 하니 이점도 참고하십시오. 구매하고 한달도 채 안돼 프로라는 명칭으로 제품이 출시되었으며 정품등록은 그 제품부터 가능하다고 합니다. 이 제품도 AS는 구입일 시점으로 적용한다고는 하나 정품등록이 안된다고 하니 마음은 불편하네요. 이후 건조기도 구매했는데 정말 미닉스 제품 정이 뚝 떨어졌습니다.

Sentence (English): This is my first time owning a dishwasher so I don't have much experience to compare it to however I have used them in the past and this one is pretty great if you ask me.
Comments (English): [ Great! ] || ---------------- || This is my first time owning a dishwasher so I don't have much experience to compare it to however I have used them in the past and this one is pretty great if you ask me. I've had it now for a few months and use the quantum finish pod detergents and their fluid rinse/dry product and my dishes come out perfect nearly every time even if food remains or particles have been on the dishes for a few days prior to running it. I have very hard water here where I live so I have noticed water marks on black pots and pans after running but it's easily removed with a paper towel and kitchen cloth and it doesn't happen to the dishes just the pots/pans however I plan to get some of the softening salts to use so this issue isn't Bosch's fault it's just the hard water in my area. The dishwasher is pretty quiet, it's spacious and I love all the different cleaning modes including the ability to do a delayed wash start. One more critique I have for Bosch would be to automatically turn on the energy saving auto shut off feature after the cycle has run, instead the washer stays on indefinitely until you press the power button or change the settings which is easy to do but it's not easy to know that there even are settings you can change. Thank goodness I read all the manuals and documents that came with, as I usually don't if it's a straight forward thing product I've used before. It also seems not so green friendly to not have that feature automatically turned on esp when they company makes so many environmental claims. To me the wash cycles also take very long I think the shortest cycle is just under 2 hours,but maybe that's how long all my dishwashers take I'm not sure,and dishes come out clean so I shouldn't complain. Overall I love this dishwasher and even with the small complaints mentioned above I still give it a 5 and recommend!

Sentence (English): We are loving this machine!
Comments (English): [ Great to use, confusing instructions ] || ---------------- || We are loving this machine! There is a learning curve with some of the instructions. Some things are a bit vague in the instructions. Also, I still can't seem to understand how to know when I am low on rinse aid. However, the machine itself is very quiet. I wish it didn't take two hours to wash a load. But at least I can plan for that and have it wash when I go to bed or when I leave in the morning and then unload first thing in the morning or after lunch. The remote control app and notifications are fun, but other than the novelty of that feature, I really don't need to use it. We mainly just wash the dishes on the normal setting or automatic setting and everything comes out beautifully clean and shiny. We did end up melting one plastic wine glass not realizing it couldn't handle it. For now, we still wash our Tupperware and plasticware by hand. But the majority of our dishes go in. For two people, we find that the tiny size is actually more than enough for our needs. It also is saving water compared to when we hand washed everything.

The second tray has two height adjustments that both fail; the high option is too high and cannot place bottles in the "bottle rinser" section. The lower option is so low the spinning water dispenser hits the plates and even utensils. The bottom tray has half the tines (for the racks) straight up instead of the usual slight tilt that keeps plates from knocking into each other. And worse, the cleaning pods gets only half diluted; so when the dishwasher is done, there is still half the pod in the dispenser. Overall, I am surpised this machine made it through to production and am sad I had to live with it for another 5 years.

Sentence (English): This is our first dishwasher and we are very pleased.
Comments (English): [ Great features, great looks ] || ---------------- || This is our first dishwasher and we are very pleased. We were looking for an option that had a metal body and had an automatic door opening feature because we planned to run it mostly in the evenings so they could dry out nicely by morning. With this model, the wish came true. The workmanship is very high quality. The most important thing is that the dishes shine with cleanliness, and the machine is quite quiet. Shows the remaining time of the cycle. Additional programs can be set up via a mobile app. There is also a short program of 1 hour. The third basket for cutlery is also a convenience, which saves space. The color is dark stainless steel, which looks very stylish. We recommend both for function and look.
Comments (Original): [ Отлични функции, отлична визия ] || ---------------- || Това ни е първата съдомиялна и сме много доволни. Търсехме вариант, който да е с метален корпус и да има функция за автоматично отваряне на вратата, защото планирахме да я пускаме предимно вечер и да могат да изсъхнат хубаво до сутринта. С този модел желанието се изпълни. Изработката е много качествена. Най-важното е, че съдовете светят от чистота, а и машината е доста тиха. Показва оставащото време от цикъла. Може да се настройват допълнителни програми през мобилно приложение. Има и кратка програма от 1 час. Удобство е и третата кошница за прибори, която пести място. Цветът е тъмен инокс, който стои много стилно. Препоръчваме както като фукнция, така и като визия.

Sentence (English): I wanted a dishwasher that was freestanding (this one can also be built in).
Comments (English): [ Very satisfied ] || ---------------- || I wanted a dishwasher that was freestanding (this one can also be built in). It had to be a dishwasher that I could rely on. That's why I chose the Bosch SMS2HVI02E. I'm very happy with it. It washes very quietly and cleanly. The WiFi connection and setup were very easy, as were the instructions for the device. The inlet and outlet hoses fit exactly without extensions. My dishwasher is about 2 m from the drain. The Home Connect app always notifies me when the program has ended or when something needs to be refilled, for example. The last 30 minutes of each program are used for drying. I'm also very happy that I can start it remotely using the app. In my opinion, it's the best dishwasher I could have.
Comments (Original): [ Sehr zufrieden ] || ---------------- || Ich habe mir einen Geschirrspüler gewünscht, welcher freistehend (dieser hier kann auch verbaut werden) ist. Mein Geschirrspüler steht ca. 2 m vom Abfluss entfernt. Über die App Home-Connect werde ich stets benachrichtigt, wenn das Programm endete oder bspw. etwas nachgefüllt werden müsse. Bei jedem Programm werden die letzten 30 Minuten für das Trocknen genutzt. Was mich auch sehr erfreut, dass ich ihn über die App aus der Ferne starten kann. Für mich der beste Geschirrspüler, den ich haben kann.

Sentence (English): I decided on taking a chance with the KitchenAid dishwasher over buying another Bosch dishwasher as they have gone up a decent amount in price.
Comments (English): [ Poor performance ] || ---------------- || I decided on taking a chance with the KitchenAid dishwasher over buying another Bosch dishwasher as they have gone up a decent amount in price. But I am nothing but disappointed in the performance and longevity of this product. We purchased this in Nov '22 and were already questioning its performance when we did our first few loads, everything was still quite wet; versus our previous DW would dry everything immaculately. We try adding a rinse aid to help with the drying as well as messing around with the heated dry option, but things still come out wet. I now have to run the dishwasher overnight and let it sit for a while before unloading or using a kitchen towel to dry off pretty much everything. Towards the end of the 'warranty' period the finger proof coating has started to peel at the bottom and there are a few rust spots there, as well as at the steam vent above the handle. I tried calling, but this isn't in the warranty any way as it is not a 'functional' issue. The best they could do was offer me a discount for another product of theirs-no thanks! I also purchased the more expensive version thinking it would preform better and have better drying capabilities, but I was wrong! I'm also dumbfounded that this dishwasher doesn't have a child lock setting since the bottons are all touch sensored, but the cheaper DW from them has a child lock setting. Overall, I would not recommend this product to anyone! Huge waste of almost $1000. I would recommend spending a few hundred more and getting the Bosh, it was extremely quiet and everything would be dried. I never write reviews, but I hope this helps others make the right choice and not choose this for just an aesthetic look.

Comments (English): [ faulty track and wheels ] || ---------------- || Absolutely disappointed with Bosch. After much research, many customers have complained that there is an engineering error and the wheels are too small causing the problem. I asked for a manager to explain the "known" problem to see if I could just get a set of wheels sent to me. The agent refused to transfer me to a manager and continued only to offer me a $180.00 service call. I am disgusted that I purchased a more expensive dishwasher with the Bosch name only to find out how poor customer service is and how bad the products are. A $1200.00 dishwasher should not malfunction after 2 years and should be engineered with great precision. Very disappointed.

But since I can't use the storage feature, I'm stuck with pre-washing, adding a little detergent, and running it on the standard + storage cycle. The cutlery rack is ok, however it takes effort to place the cutlery in it so that they sit sideways and don’t flip out of the slots. Sentence (English): I really like our new GE© Dishwasher.
Comments (English): [ 24 GAL/11 Min of handwashing VS 4 GAL/1 Dishwasher ] || ---------------- || I really like our new GE© Dishwasher. Our old Dishwasher had pieces falling off, but it was a least 10yrs old. The new GE© Dishwasher has three racks, with the highest very shallow rack having space for cookie sheets or plastic container lids saving space on the bottom rack for larger pots and dinner plates. The middle rack (what would have been the top rack in our old Dishwasher) has four bottle jets with clips to keep them in place! I also love the all in one silverware basket. It has three sections. Two sections on either end with their own snap down covers with room for ten pieces of silverware and at the back of these sections are two slots perfect for knives. The middle section of the silverware basket has a single snap down cover but this is subdivided into three sections with slots at the back for knives and at the left and right ends are spaces for larger items like spatulas. The cool thing about this middle section that has a single snap down cover and subdividen into three sections allows you to place at least two sharp steak, slicing or chopping knives separated from the other silverware. This keeps the sharp knifes from getting hit or rubbed by the other pieces of silverware and prevents the sharp knives from getting dull. The GE© Dishwasher uses FOUR GALLONS of water per ONE Dishwasher cycle VS TWENTY-FOUR GALLONS of water with ELEVEN MINUTES of handwashing dishes! This is the BEST Dishwasher hands down that I have ever had!

Sentence (English): I did research for my needs and 10 year planning of my kitchen.
Comments (English): [ Dont bother unless you've updated your kitchen ] || ---------------- || I did research for my needs and 10 year planning of my kitchen. As someone who literally spends many hours in the kitchen, I want the bells and whistles. The Cafe had those bells and whistles from the knock pause feature, 2 separate drawers, ADA like complaint drawers, and even highlights its ability to wash china. I cant even use it because of a HUGE failure on the manufactures part is not allowing the power source to be customizable or the option for hardwire vs plug-in. I even paid for the matte black finished bars, and extra $300 to customize my kitchen for its color theme. I now have 2 unusable dishwashers, an unusable kitchen, and have to make a rash choice in giving up my dream dishwasher or do a mad dash of calls for an electrician. While if I had purchased the GE Profile I was looking at that was MORE expensive has "Optional cord kit (GPFCORD - WX09X70910, WX09X70911)" even the Café™ CustomFit ENERGY STAR Stainless Interior Smart Dishwasher with Ultra Wash & Dry, 42 dBA even shows "Optional cord kit (GPFCORD - WX09X70910, WX09X70911)"They launched the same line with 2 different power sources and believed it was obvious to a new home owner.

Sentence (English): I bought a Bosch thinking that I'd never have to worry about my two most common dishwashing problems again: items not drying and food remaining on the dishes.
Comments (English): [ Best dishwasher I've had, but still has issues ] || ---------------- || I bought a Bosch thinking that I'd never have to worry about my two most common dishwashing problems again: items not drying and food remaining on the dishes. This Bosch is far and away better than my old dishwasher on both issues, but I do occasionally finish a cycle and find wet or dirty dishes. So it's better, but not perfect. Additionally, I've had a few disposable plastic containers melted and there's no way to turn down the heat. I appreciate the app, because through it I learned that if you run a shortened 60 minute cycle (which is what I was doing, thinking that it uses less water and energy), it actually uses more energy than a Normal 2 hour cycle. I've had fewer plastic melting issues since switching to the Normal cycle. The last comment is that the racks in this dishwasher are also far better than my last dishwasher. Because of their design, items naturally fall into a slanted position that lessens the likelihood of water pooling. However, these racks are not as adjustable as the more expensive models, and one example of this is the spacing between the plate separators. On this model, they're too fine to accommodate my plates efficiently. I've seen other Bosch racks where that spacing is adjustable.

Sentence (English): We purchased a 24 inch bosch 10 years ago.
Comments (English): [ The Microsoft Word of dishwashers ] || ---------------- || We purchased a 24 inch bosch 10 years ago. It's brilliant! And the user interface is completely intuitive. Ten years later, we figured Bosch would be a good choice. The dishes come out great! The drying function is top of the class. BUT - to operate the machine I had to call the appliance store, watch at least three Youtube videos, and there are still features that are a mystery to me. It reminds me of Microsoft. They had to keep updated their Office apps. They didn't need to. They just did. They became unrecognizable. There is no consistency from my old Bosch (still have it) to my new one. Finally, if you need to download an app to access some features, the design engineers failed in their job.

Sentence (English): Kind of regret this purchase.
Comments (English): Kind of regret this purchase. 5 out of 10 times dishes will come out completely wet still, despite the highest dry setting used and rinse aid. Also entire dishes and bowls will still be dirty for seemingly no explanation, even though it's loaded correctly and soap is loaded fine. It's superficial stuck dirt I can literally blow off with my mourh once I take it out. Why didn't the dishwasher take it off? Who knows. This dishwasher really pushes the detergent pods on you, but I found out the pod doesn't completely dissolve sometimes and you're left with plastic melted on a dish or two. Since switching to gel this doesn't happen. Third rack is nothing special. It also doesn't clean things most of the time. The bottle jets are a gimmick. No adult sized bottle will fit on them, leaving you to have to remove the third rack to get the 2nd rack to close. Overall for then price I'm extremely disappointed in the performance. A note about HD delivery and setup. They installed it, but it's crooked in my space. It's supposed to be a top controls unit but it looks so bad installed crooked. Sigh.

Sentence (English): First, we purchased this product at Home Depot.
Comments (English): [ Nice unit. until it fails ] || ---------------- || First, we purchased this product at Home Depot. Our purchase included a Dishwasher, Refrigerator, and a self-cleaning convection oven. All GE, all the same style. I loved this dishwasher. It was so much better than the previous unit and the third shelf and the bottle jets were the tops. However, it lasted only about 5 years. We purchased in 2019 and it is dead, for the second time, today.About three months ago, it started to make the same three-note-noise that it makes when you opened the dishwasher door. To be clear, this would happen when the door was closed. Just sitting around the house and the chime kicks off about once every 15 to 20 minutes. Just over and over and over. All day. Then, one day, it was dead.I pulled it out, tested the power outlet and all was good there. Plugged it back in and nothing. Started my research and found the control board to be the most likely culprit. In fact, there was little else available online that pointed to anything else. Anyway, found the part on GE's website, ordered it and installed it myself. Everything worked fine with the new part, except the darned "door open" chiming continued. Whatever, I figured it was a door sensor or something.Less than a month after buying and installing the new part, the dishwasher has failed again. I called GE support and the lady on the phone was polite and courteous, but all that can be done is to send a service technician, for about $115 and then, of course, whatever they find will be additional cost. Not sure yet if we will go that route or buy another dishwasher (likely a different model) or just go without for a while.I am quite disappointed. Items like this should last much longer than 5 years. I had a builder grade dishwasher in place for more than 15 years and while it lacked any modern features and was quite a bit louder than this one, it worked - every time - and was in working condition when we replaced it.Super unfortunate and I wish GE would simply replace it. I mean come on, already. It failed for reasons that seem to have everything to do with component quality. Basically, from the day I purchased this item, it was destined to fail.

At one point I was wondering why the inside of the dishwasher was still damp and as it turned out, I received a notification that the rinse aid was low. Comments (English): [ Bosch 800 Series Model #SHX78CM6N ] || ---------------- || We have had this for over 2 months with a few things I would change about this dishwasher and the process. (1) The power connecting cord is NOT US standard appliance connecting cord & NOT direct hardwire connection either, so if your electrical connection is over 4' to the outlet, you will need to purchase optional BOSCH junction box. (2) There is no Clean indication for completed cycle. It would be nice if the Red Floor indicator for active washing could turn Green and stay Green until door is opened. [I use “Dirty/Clean' magnet for others in the house to be aware of this, but it takes away from the clean aesthetic of the front door that I was after]. (3) Although the rack layout is not something we in the US are accustomed to, it does have some nice factures with some flaws [still trying get the quantity of dishes my 11-year-old KitchenAid dishwasher could do]. (4) It is extremely quiet--I mean "really" quiet -- and it shows a solid red light on the floor when it's running so you can see that it's running at a glance. Its interior modular design is great for different sized items from pots and pans to small silverware. Overall, it is very easy to use even though 90% of the time I just use "Auto" with heavy spray mode in all 4 sections. Even with its faults, it's ahead of my old dishwasher. I would buy it again just for the quiet, cleaning, & drying operation.

Sentence (English): Despite the brand and having a previous model, this one has disappointed me a lot in terms of the drying system it has and in customer service they recognize that the new models are thus less efficient in drying (total design failure in my opinion ).
Comments (English): [ Very bad drying in plastics ] || ---------------- || Despite the brand and having a previous model, this one has disappointed me a lot in terms of the drying system it has and in customer service they recognize that the new models are thus less efficient in drying (total design failure in my opinion ). It doesn't matter what program you put it on and what settings you have, even with extra drying. The plastics and the dishwasher itself get very wet and the problem is not that, but that having those drops, they will cause mold or a musty smell over time. As you can see in the photos, any plastic thing gets very wet, and those drops will fall on your dishes, so either you take out the recently finished dishes (forget to put it at night then) or you find your dishes with drip marks. or even wet.

Da igual el programa en que lo pongas y las configuraciones que tengas, incluso con extra secado. Comments (English): [ Very bad drying on plastics ] || ---------------- || Despite the brand and having a previous model, this one has disappointed me quite a bit in terms of the drying system it has and customer service recognises that the new models are like that, less efficient in drying (total design failure in my opinion). It doesn't matter what programme you put it on and what settings you have, even with extra drying. The plastics and the dishwasher itself get very wet and the problem is not that, but that having those drops will cause mould or a damp smell over time. As you can see in the photos, anything made of plastic gets very wet, and those drops will fall on your dishes, so either you take out the fresh dishes when they are finished (forget about putting them on at night then) or you find your dishes with drip marks or even wet.

Da igual el programa en que lo pongas y las configuraciones que tengas, incluso con extra secado. Los plasticos y el propio lavavajillas quedan mojadisimo y el problema no es es, sino que al tener esas gotas, causaran moho u olor a humedad con el tiempo. Como se ve en las fotos cualquier cosas de plasticos queda muy mojado, y esas gotas caeran en tu vajilla, por lo que o sacas la vajilla reciente terminado (olvidate de ponerlo por las noches entonces) o tu vajilla te la encuentras con marcas de gotas o incluso mojado.

Comments (English): [ Quiet Cleans Well ] || ---------------- || We bought this to replace our 20 year old Whirlpool dishwasher that needed replacing. This new Whirlpool is a lot quieter than the old one (the old one was pretty quiet). We can't really hear it at all while it is on. It cleans dishes, and pots and pans very well, without any food cast off, full disclosure, we wipe or do a quick rinse of heavier foods or baked on foods first. I have really never seen a dishwasher that completely eliminates cast off. We are pleased with the third tray. It handles all of our silverware and cooking utensils. We do not use the silverware baskets as the third tray handles all the silverware and utensils we use. We haven't had a large family gathering yet, I am sure we will need to use the silverware baskets when the whole gang comes (20+ kids, spouses and grandkids). We also like the height adjustable feature on the second tray. We can fit our tallest pots and pans without any problems. With the utensil basket out the is extra room for more dishes. Overall, we are very pleased with the quietness, capacity and cleaning ability of the dishwasher. The is a quick one hour cycle other than that the other cycles are a bit long at three hours. For us the length of the cycles are not an issue. This is a great dishwasher that seems to be well built and should last a long time. Hopefully, we'll 20 years out of it like we did our first Whirlpool dishwasher.

Sentence (English): This is the ABSOLUTE WORST dishwasher I have ever owned.
Comments (English): [ DO NOT BUY Flooding/Falls Apart/Doesn't Clean ] || ---------------- || This is the ABSOLUTE WORST dishwasher I have ever owned. THE. WORST. Purchased this as a matching set for our home, which we are getting ready to sell. 1. Leak issues: This DW has flooded out kitchen at least five times now. Our recently refinished wood floors are completely ruined. There are two causes of flooding. The first is due to the upper rack washer arm falling off and blocking the lower washer arm (see below). The second is due to the tines on the lower rack become unlocked from the spray of the water. The clips that are supposed to hold the tines are weak and the force of the lower water spray knocks them loose so that they swing down into the bottom path of the washer bar. We have had to use cable ties to lock these into place. This is not a loading or user issue - this is a mechanical/design issue. DO NOT RUN THIS DW UNLESS YOU ARE ABLE TO MONITOR IT DURING THE ENTIRE CYCLE! 2. Nearly EVERY DAY the washer arm on the top rack falls off and needs to be reconnected. Nothing is blocking the rotation of the washer arm and it is always re-installed properly. It just falls off. Sometimes this blocks the lower wash arm and results in flooding. 3.Poor interior design. The bottom rack doesn't have tines going across the entire rack. Nor does it have a full grid on the bottom rack. This results in large gaps which allows items to down into the path of the washer bar, which results in (wait for it) flooding and/or dishes not getting clean. Even the silverware container drops into the gap or falls over because of the lack of a stable area to put it on. 4. Items on the uppermost third rack don't get fully clean. Only the undersides will get clean - and that's if items on the glass rack are not blocking them. This third rack is useless if you need to depend on something getting cleaned and sanitized. We have stopped using it. 5.Drying is sporadic. Sometimes this dries everything well, sometimes it leaves items (and not just plastic) wet. No idea why this happens. We use the same cycle every time and generally wash the same items each day. The only positives about this DW are that it is relatively quiet and it matches the other appliances. Because we have to monitor this DW during operation, we can't leave the house, run it at bedtime or use it at any time that is convenient for us. We must stay nearby to check every 10-15 minutes, as flooding and leaking can occur at any point of the wash cycle. Do yourself a favor. Buy something else!

Sentence (English): There was a built-in dishwasher in my previous house, but I didn't like its cleaning power and it was big so I didn't use it much, so I didn't install it when I moved and did the interior design this time.
Comments (English): [ It's comfortable ] || ---------------- || There was a built-in dishwasher in my previous house, but I didn't like its cleaning power and it was big so I didn't use it much, so I didn't install it when I moved and did the interior design this time. However, I have trigger finger syndrome and elbows these days, so it's hard to wash dishes, so I searched for a dishwasher and found a product I had been eyeing on Coupang that was being sold very cheaply, so I quickly ordered it. I even got a card discount, but it's being sold for more now that I've checked (oh yeah^^) It's a small size, but it's just right for washing dishes after a basic meal for a family of three. The cleaning power is good and I really like that the door opens after it's done. It doesn't use hot air drying, but it dries to 70-80% and if you leave it with the door open, it seems to slowly turn into a dryer. My kitchen is not that small, so it's a bit stuffy when I put it on top, but I guess it'll be okay once I get used to it^^; I hope you use this product well. I used the drying mode in the evening and the next morning, the inside of the dishwasher was completely dry^^

Comments (English): I was very worried about buying a dishwasher, but I ended up choosing this product. First of all, the installer came and installed it kindly and well. I wondered how many dishes it would hold because it was small, but it was the perfect size for our family of four. The first worry I had when using a dishwasher was whether it would clean properly. It cleaned everything from the scissors, tongs, oil pan, and plates that were covered in grease after grilling pork belly. At first, I didn't use rinse and just used GoCheck detergent, but there were a lot of stains. So I used rinse together, and the stains disappeared a lot and it was clean. I've been using it for about a month and a half now, and the only downside is that it takes a little bit of time. It usually takes 50 minutes once and 1 hour and 10 minutes on strong mode. But I can't believe how happy I am to escape the dishwashing hell without doing the dishes. I highly recommend buying a dishwasher if you're worried about the size because it'll only increase your dishwashing hell.^^

Sentence (English): This dishwasher.
Comments (English): [ There are a lot of features to get use to. ] || ---------------- || This dishwasher. works well, I am still adjusting to how it runs. I am not used to the controls being on the top edge of the door, hidden when the dishwasher is closed. I am also still testing out the different cycles to see how they clean, and how long they run, I am of the old school where you don't run the dishwasher till it is full. So I have only used it three times since it was installed. This dishwasher is very quiet when running, so I often have to put my ear up close to make sure it is running. It blocks the use of one drawer and one cupboard door now that it is installed. I had to remove the cupboard door to access the cupboard itself. (It is a large, deep cupboard for storing large appliances you don't use regularly that take up too much space on the counter to leave out.) For the drawer I have to open the dishwasher and lay the door down to open the drawer. so this is now where I store my extra knives. As a gift, I can't complain too much I wish the givers would have remembered that the Dishwasher goes in a corner slot in the kitchen and had purchased one designed for a corner. The adjustable racks, the top rack for cutlery and utensils, and the separate silverware basket are nice features. However some of my silverware slides right through the slots on the basket top. making the top useless when trying to wash salad forks and teaspoons. which are half the size of the dinner forks and dessert spoons.

Pros: what few dishes I can fit in come out clean, even though I have to do 2 loads instead of 1 with my previous machine. It's super quiet and even on auto it's faster than my old dishwasher. Detailed review: I hate this machine. And I've waited months to write this review in order to give it a fair shot and also get over the “change” of a new machine. We had our old Kitchen Aid for nearly 15 years—unheard of nowadays! —and I knew switching to a new machine, while more powerful and quieter, would be painful. My hope was the pros (as aforementioned, SO much more quieter, more power, and overall generally cleaner dishes) would outweigh the cons. After months of using this on a daily, sometimes twice daily basis, I can confirm it doesn't. I want my old Kitchen Aid back. The cons seem silly—except I'm fighting with inanimate objects multiple times a day. The top rack—new to me and super fiddly to have to lay out each piece of silverware—but I can't deny it gets them ~98% clean where the basket often has/had issues with food occasionally get stuck at the bottom or between pieces. Using the silverware separator/lid helps but is such an inefficient use of space, so we've removed the basket and only use the top rack. It's a time suck but I'm ok since the silverware comes out clean nearly all the time. The middle and bottom rack are the problems. Because of the space taken up by the top tray, neither the middle OR the bottom—even with the adjustable middle rack—can easily fit my dishes. Our standard size cereal bowls and wine glasses will only fit in the middle if completely dropped to the lowest level—and the wine glasses have water pooling/drying in the side of the bowl because they are so horizontal. Which means I can't fit a dinner plate—or even a cutting board on the bottom. So then I raise the middle rack—which means bowls, salad plates, dinner plates all have to fit on the bottom—which leaves zero room for any serving or cooking dishes. Again, the middle rack is doable. We can finagle to use the space mostly efficiently. The biggest annoyance is the bottom rack. The Bosch designers 100% missed the boat on the bottom rack design. If I could still return this dishwasher, I would, solely because of how annoying this bottom rack is. There is no track or decent guides along the door of the machine, so unless you are standing squarely in front of the door and sliding the bottom rack out perfectly perpendicular to the counter, the rack slides all over the door. Every. Single. Time. Pain on the way out—but fairly adjustable. Downright infuriating and difficult to lift and adjust and get centered EXACTLY in the middle of the door WITH NO TRACKS when it's now full of dirty, heavy dishes. There is zero space for a large cutting board to be upright and it's foolish to have it lay horizontal and use the whole bottom rack for 1-2 dishes. The circular turntable plate from the microwave is too tall to slide in anywhere, even with adjustments. Same with a pizza pan, toaster oven pan, 1/2 baking sheet, or the wine glasses if we try not to use the horizontal middle rack option…you see my point. These aren't specialty dishes. Who doesn't use a microwave or make pizzas? The back row of prongs are a bit narrow and too angular which only lends itself to plates and lids only—zero flexibility for any other kind of dish (but in their defense, the plates and plastic lids DO come out clean). The front half has awkward spacing that doesn't fit any of my (Pyrex and nesting serving/mixing bowls, typical and common dishes—not even including my non-US items like ramen/rice/soup bowls in this review since I don't think it's fair to compare since this machine is designed for a US market—but funny how my Kitchen Aid could handle a lot more flexibility and therefore quantity of dishes per load). We chose the controls on the top instead of front. I thought it would be more convenient, easier to read, etc. I'm still mostly ok with that, though the sensitivity the touch buttons leaves something to be desired. When you brush against the top with a leg while you're loading dishes, it turns on. Yet when I want to change the settings, turn on/reset/start I have to push the buttons multiple times. I can't believe I'm saying it, but I'd rather go back decades and have a dial than this horrible touchscreen. There are a bunch of new options with this machine. Except the app isn't great at defining or telling you the difference between settings. It's more interested in selling additional services or recipes. I tried again to see if I could easily find a legend of all the symbols in the window. What a joke. Still looking. And switching from one setting (auto to quick to heavy, etc) to another never works, the sensitivity of the touch/buttons is not there. Half the time I'm forced to go to the app to do a hard stop/cancel. It's seriously annoying to have to use an app to use my dishwasher. Overall, knowing what I know now, I would've done more research on the physical unit instead of relying so much on reviews and ratings. Yes, it's quiet, washes well, and is efficient on energy. But it's a pain to use and wastes my time and energy since I have to do extra loads to get the same amount as my previous machine.

My hope was the pros (as aforementioned, SO much more quieter, more power, and overall generally cleaner dishes) would outweigh the cons. After months of using this on a daily, sometimes twice daily basis, I can confirm it doesn’t. I want my old Kitchen Aid back. The cons seem silly—except I’m fighting with inanimate objects multiple times a day. The top rack—new to me and super fiddly to have to lay out each piece of silverware—but I can’t deny it gets them ~98% clean where the basket often has/had issues with food occasionally get stuck at the bottom or between pieces. Using the silverware separator/lid helps but is such an inefficient use of space, so we’ve removed the basket and only use the top rack. It’s a time suck but I’m ok since the silverware comes out clean nearly all the time. The middle and bottom rack are the problems. Because of the space taken up by the top tray, neither the middle OR the bottom—even with the adjustable middle rack—can easily fit my dishes. Our standard size cereal bowls and wine glasses will only fit in the middle if completely dropped to the lowest level—and the wine glasses have water pooling/drying in the side of the bowl because they are so horizontal. Which means I can’t fit a dinner plate—or even a cutting board on the bottom. So then I raise the middle rack—which means bowls, salad plates, dinner plates all have to fit on the bottom—which leaves zero room for any serving or cooking dishes. Again, the middle rack is doable. We can finagle to use the space mostly efficiently. The biggest annoyance is the bottom rack. The Bosch designers 100% missed the boat on the bottom rack design. If I could still return this dishwasher, I would, solely because of how annoying this bottom rack is. There is no track or decent guides along the door of the machine, so unless you are standing squarely in front of the door and sliding the bottom rack out perfectly perpendicular to the counter, the rack slides all over the door. Every. Single. Time. Pain on the way out—but fairly adjustable. Downright infuriating and difficult to lift and adjust and get centered EXACTLY in the middle of the door WITH NO TRACKS when it’s now full of dirty, heavy dishes. There is zero space for a large cutting board to be upright and it’s foolish to have it lay horizontal and use the whole bottom rack for 1-2 dishes. The circular turntable plate from the microwave is too tall to slide in anywhere, even with adjustments. Same with a pizza pan, toaster oven pan, 1/2 baking sheet, or the wine glasses if we try not to use the horizontal middle rack option…you see my point. These aren’t specialty dishes. Who doesn’t use a microwave or make pizzas?!  The back row of prongs are a bit narrow and too angular which only lends itself to plates and lids only—zero flexibility for any other kind of dish (but in their defense, the plates and plastic lids DO come out clean). The front half has awkward spacing that doesn’t fit any of my (Pyrex and nesting serving/mixing bowls, typical and common dishes—not even including my non-US items like ramen/rice/soup bowls in this review since I don’t think it’s fair to compare since this machine is designed for a US market—but funny how my Kitchen Aid could handle a lot more flexibility and therefore quantity of dishes per load). We chose the controls on the top instead of front. I thought it would be more convenient, easier to read, etc. I’m still mostly ok with that, though the sensitivity the touch buttons leaves something to be desired. When you brush against the top with a leg while you’re loading dishes, it turns on. Yet when I want to change the settings, turn on/reset/start I have to push the buttons multiple times. I can’t believe I’m saying it, but I’d rather go back decades and have a dial than this horrible touchscreen. There are a bunch of new options with this machine. Except the app isn’t great at defining or telling you the difference between settings. It’s more interested in selling additional services or recipes. I tried again to see if I could easily find a legend of all the symbols in the window. What a joke. Still looking. And switching from one setting (auto to quick to heavy, etc) to another never works, the sensitivity of the touch/buttons is not there. Half the time I’m forced to go to the app to do a hard stop/cancel. It’s seriously annoying to have to use an app to use my dishwasher. Overall, knowing what I know now, I would’ve done more research on the physical unit instead of relying so much on reviews and ratings. Yes, it’s quiet, washes well, and is efficient on energy. But it’s a pain to use and wastes my time and energy since I have to do extra loads to get the same amount as my previous machine.

Scheduling was incredibly difficult, so I decided to look for a solution that would simply use a bucket or a water tank. After researching numerous options, I settled on the Minix. The water filler is clearly located at the bottom, making it convenient to refill after each use. Even if I need to drill a hole later, I also appreciate the ability to install a direct water connection. I purchased this dishwasher with a two-part detergent that includes rinse and detergent, and it cleans up well. I use it on standard wash mode, and the auto-open feature is nice. I hope they'll add a way to turn the auto-open feature on and off in the future. While hot air drying is nice, I prefer air drying. I used to spend a lot of time washing dishes, especially greasy ones, and I was covered in sweat every time I washed them. Having a dishwasher frees up time and allows me to focus on cooking, which I appreciate. It's not large enough to fit large pots or pans. If you're planning on washing pots and pans separately, and utensils, spoons, and cups separately, this size is incredibly helpful. The design is the best of any dishwashing set on the market right now, perfect for this size. When purchasing, choose one with a glass interior that lets you see inside. It's a great design, and it's also great for being able to see the entire dishwashing process.

Sentence (English): When we built our home over 20 years ago, we installed a Bosch dishwasher.
Comments (English): [ Excellent Dishwasher ] || ---------------- || When we built our home over 20 years ago, we installed a Bosch dishwasher. It finally died when a piece of plastic from a broken utensil damaged the recirculation motor. The part was no longer available. If the part had been available, it might have lasted another 10 years. The new dishwasher was delivered by Lowes with care, and I installed the dishwasher in less than an hour. The new 800 series dishwasher has water and power connections on the back where our previous Bosch dishwasher had the connections on the front. It comes with a power cord that fits a standard outlet. but we needed the junction box (sold separately) to connect it to our power. In hindsight, I'd have installed an outlet in the back of the dishwasher cabinet, though the junction box is fine. The third rack/tray is new for us, and we really enjoy the third tray for washing silverware, small condiment bowls, and utensils like spatulas, mixing spoons, etc. We prefer the layout of the tines and racks much better than our previous Bosch dishwasher. The 800 series layout is more versatile, so I see that as an improvement. The tines are thinner, but that is a benefit as it allows more items to be added to the same space. Some tines fold down for even more customization. The smaller utensil basket makes sense with the third rack being used primarily for this purpose. We may eventually remove the small basket completely. One thing I noticed right away was that the middle rack seemed very loose with side-to-side play compared to our previous Bosch dishwasher, and this at first seemed like less precision and less durable construction, but then I realized the middle rack has the ability to be canted with one side higher/lower than the other to accommodate tall pots or pans in the lower basket. This is a nice design feature that I think often flies under the radar for most that own this dishwasher. I'm assuming that some of the play in the middle rack is due to this greater adjustment ability. The height adjustment feet in front and the adjustable rear foot set by turning a screw on the front is brilliant. It made leveling the unit so easy! The one thing I view as a negative is the front door. The brushed steel skin flexes easily when pressed. This feels cheap and doesn't match a premium dishwasher. The front door also flexes from side to side and could easily be twisted. The door simply needs more reinforcement. Our previous Bosch, which was a lower-end model at the time, had a much sturdier door.I like the white light when running better than the red LED projected onto the floor. Frankly, that red LED light would drive our Jack Russell insane. He doesn't notice the white LED on the door panel.The unit isn't quite as quiet as I was expecting. We do have our unit installed in a cabinet with hardwood floors and butcherblock countertop, and perhaps this creates an acoustic cabinet that amplifies the sound. I will likely pull the dishwasher back out, add some additional sound insulation, and then re-install it. As some reviews have stated and I agree, the responsiveness of the controls could be improved. Sometimes it takes a couple of tries to register my selections. But, honestly. now that I've tested the various options for awhile, 99% of the time I will simply press Start, so this isn't a concern for me.The dishes, glassware, stainless cups, pots and pans, and utensils have come out pristine using Cascade Platinum with the Bosch 800. We don't wash much plastic, so I turned off Crystal Dry and will only use it when washing plastic. Overall, I'm very happy with the dishwasher and hope it has a long life like our last Bosch.
